title: Member Accounting Memo: Capital Credit Retirement Credits Applied to a Payment Arrangements Payoff
content:
**Member accounting memo — Capital Credits (Patronage Capital) retirement credits and Payment Arrangements (Deferred Payment Agreements) payoffs**

**Rule.** Capital credit retirement credits among the bill credits considered at an early payoff are applied to the payoff according to the member's Capital Credits (Patronage Capital) account in the patron class of the service account's rate schedule, as it stands on the payoff day:

- at 100 percent (1.0) of their amount where that capital credit account is active and has been open at least 300 calendar months on the payoff day;
- at 50 percent (0.5) of their amount where it is active and has been open fewer months;
- not at all where the member holds no active capital credit account.

**Records read.** The patron class is the one into which the service account's rate schedule allocates patronage. The account's status and its opened date are read from the member's capital credit records; months open are counted in calendar months from the opened date to the payoff day. 300 calendar months are twenty-five years.

| Capital credit account in the patron class | Months open on the payoff day | Share of the retirement credits applied |
|---|---|---|
| active | 300 or more | 100 percent |
| active | fewer than 300 | 50 percent |
| not active, or none held | — | none |

**Hypothetical:** capital credit retirement credits of $64.00 among the credits considered are applied as $64.00 for a Farm Patron Class account opened 340 months before the payoff day, as $32.00 for one opened 96 months before, and not at all for a member whose account in the class is no longer active.
